correctness.rationale: The Gaussian residual vector is isotropic in the n-1 dimensional zero-sum subspace. Radial-angular independence and the chi moment ratio E[Q^(p+2)]/E[Q^p]=n-1+p give the homogeneous covariance law exactly. For MAD, its mean follows from the marginal residual variance; its variance follows from the exact absolute-product moment of an equicorrelated Gaussian pair. The n=2 boundary and large-n limit agree with the same constant 1/sqrt(pi-2).

value.rationale: Mean absolute deviation and variance are standard competing dispersion measures. The finding gives their exact finite Gaussian coupling, rather than only separate efficiencies or asymptotics, and the broader homogeneous-functional law explains the mechanism structurally. The correlation remains near 0.94 even asymptotically, quantifying substantial redundancy between linear-loss and quadratic-loss scale summaries.
